openingBrief.title: A Trip from Chicago to Boston

blocks.text: You’re planning a solo trip from Chicago O’Hare (ORD) to Boston Logan (BOS). You’ll start by comparing ways the chatbot could help you choose a flight across four scenarios that vary by budget and departure flexibility. Then you’ll move on to hotels. All flight budgets include taxes and one checked bag.

You’ll compare ways the chatbot could help you choose a hotel, room, and rate for a three-night stay in Boston. The four scenarios vary by budget and stay dates. All hotel budgets cover the full stay, including taxes and fees. Your flight answers don’t affect these tasks.

You’ll compare ways the chatbot could help you choose a rental car, pickup location, and dates for a three-day rental in Boston. The four scenarios vary by budget and rental dates. All budgets cover the full rental, including taxes and mandatory fees.
For this part, a flight, hotel, and rental car have already been picked for you. You’ll decide how to get each reservation ready for checkout.

For example, once you’ve picked a flight, the airline’s booking page might ask for your passenger details, your seat choice, and how many bags you’ll check. You could fill in those details yourself, ask the assistant to fill them in for you to review, or let the assistant handle the setup on its own.
You’ll also decide what to do if the assistant runs into a problem while preparing a reservation.

Imagine you’ve reviewed your reservation and the total, and you’re ready to pay. You’ll decide who should submit the payment and when you’d want to confirm it. You’ll also decide what to do if the assistant runs into an error at checkout.

instructions.introduction:
Imagine you’re planning and booking a trip with an AI assistant that can compare flights, hotels, and rental cars, set up reservations, and pay for you. We’re interested in which parts you’d want help with, how you’d want the assistant to help, and which parts you’d do yourself. We’re also interested in what you’d do if the assistant couldn’t complete a task.

You’ll work through scenarios based on common travel booking tasks. Use the budget, schedule flexibility, and travel preferences in each scenario to decide what kind of help would work best for you. The study has three parts.

steps.title: Planning your trip:
steps.text: Compare ways the assistant could help you choose a flight, hotel package, or rental car. You’ll see four scenarios for each booking type, with varying budgets and schedule flexibility.

steps.title: Preparing your reservations:
steps.text: Decide how much help you’d want setting up each reservation before checkout. For a flight, that could include entering passenger details, choosing a seat, and adding checked bags.

steps.title: Completing the purchase:
steps.text: Decide who you’d want to submit payment and when you’d want to confirm it.

instructions.note: For each scenario, imagine the travel preferences described are your own. Choose the response that best matches how you’d want the assistant to help.
